question: Can the pinned statement be proved on a 101 MB stock CUDA image, with sshd installed at boot instead of baked into an image?
answer: Yes, and the startup is the win. Every layer of nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-base-ubuntu24.04 was already on the machine, so the pull took 2 s; the container installed sshd and was ready 22 s after create, against ~112 s to ssh.direct on the PyTorch image. The proof is the same proof: 82 shards, 132,029,932 bytes, the same verification key and committed digest, accepted and reloaded.

gates_on_a_base_image.libcuda_not_in_dt_needed: libcuda.so.1 never appears: cudart dlopens the driver, so the image needs no driver stub at link time

cache.why: a base image has no nvcc, so the full build key cannot match however right the binary is

cost.note: includes ~2.5 min lost to the python3-minimal failure below; a clean run of this shape is ~3.5 min, ~$0.016

comparison_with_the_pytorch_image.reading: the image does not touch proving time; 2.7% is inside the 2.6-4.2% run-to-run spread, on one run each
comparison_with_the_pytorch_image.where_the_saving_is: startup: 22 s to ready against ~112 s

defect_found.symptom: the cache probe died with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'json', the launcher read that as a cache miss, and the new nvcc guard then refused to build on a toolchain-less pod
defect_found.why_it_matters: pod-prove.sh had installed python3-minimal since the prove path was written; it had never run on an image that lacked python3, so the gap was invisible
defect_found.fix: install python3 and gate on `python3 -c 'import json'` rather than on the binary's presence

limits: one run on one card; proving time here is not a card or image comparison
the 2 s pull is a WARM machine cache: the base image's layers were already present, and a cold pull of 101 MB is not measured
the build path was not exercised on this image and cannot be: there is no nvcc. Populating the cache still needs a toolkit image
